newsitem.title: USA: Hunt for alleged Versace killer grows more bizarre.
newsitem.headline: Hunt for alleged Versace killer grows more bizarre.

text.p: The manhunt for Andrew Cunanan, accused of slaying fashion king Gianni Versace, grew more bizarre on Monday amid fears he may be working through a personal hit-list while dressing as a woman to elude a police dragnet.

The FBI, which is also seeking Cunanan for four murders in a cross-country killing spree before the Versace slaying, was sifting interviews with Cunanan's friends to tip off anyone he might have mentioned who could now be a target, an FBI spokeswoman said.

"What we are doing is sifting through what people have told us about Cunanan's offhand comments. He was apparently a very bragging person and would talk about his past and perhaps name-drop other celebrities," FBI Minneapolis spokeswoman Coleen Rowley told Reuters.

"If for some reason it surfaced that someone's name has been mentioned -- name-dropped I think is a good term -- by Cunanan, we would, for what it's worth, we would err on the side of passing that information on."

She said it was exaggerated to say the FBI was "warning" possible targets, noting that Cunanan "made up a lot of things," but said it would be "remiss" not to inform the people whose names he dropped.
Versace and Cunanan, both gay, are not known to have had any sexual contact, although they may have met at least once in San Francisco.
Investigators were still concentrating the manhunt on the south Florida area but tips were flooding in from all over the United States, Rowley said.
"We are still acting on the assumption he is probably still in south Florida because we don't believe he has access to a vehicle," she said.

In Miami Beach, police continued to piece together a record of Cunanan's movements, especially his cashing in a gold coin allegedly stolen from an earlier victim at a local pawn shop where he signed his own name and left his fingerprint eight days before Versace's death.
The pawn shop, required by law to submit records of transactions to police within 24 hours, did so. But police did not examine the record before Versace was killed on July 15.

"The system is not automated or computerized," the Miami Beach Police Department said in a statement. "For that reason, there is often a time gap between the arrival of that data from the pawn shops and entry of the information."
A volunteer counsellor at a nonprofit agency for people with AIDS and HIV said last weekend Cunanan told him earlier this year he feared he might have contracted the AIDS virus.
He quoted Cunanan as saying he would "get" whoever may have transmitted it to him. One of his previous alleged victims was a former lover.
Police said on Monday they had no concrete information that Cunanan was HIV-positive.

Hair clippings and an electric razor found at Cunanan's last known abode -- a faded hotel at the less fashionable north end of Miami Beach -- led police to issue a statement on Sunday saying Cunanan "may be dressing as a female and may have shaved all of his body hair to enhance this appearance."

The only suspect in last week's shooting death of the celebrated Italian designer, Cunanan has a history of adroitly using costumes and makeup. Investigators said he also may be wearing eyeglasses or contact lenses.

Newsweek magazine reported that a Brazilian woman told investigators she had photographs and videotape of Cunanan inside Versace's gated mansion a week ago, two days before the 50-year-old designer was killed after a visit to a newsstand.
Brazilian police concluded, however, that the people shown were not Versace and Cunanan.
